headline: High: shared broad network egress and overlapping API-key handling create default leakage and action-conflict risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter ingests external web/API content and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while kotaemon processes documents/HTML/PDFs in a web UI. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if dexter outputs are copied into kotaemon or shared via files. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF dexter outputs are copied into kotaemon documents or chat inputs, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
IF both agents read from the same shared folder, file content can become an instruction channel.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw web output into kotaemon.
Add a manual review step before importing dexter scratchpad files.
Use read-only exports for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress; kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys, and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from one agent into third-party APIs without a clear containment boundary. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default docs, so severity is high.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at the same folder containing secrets or sensitive documents, those contents may be uploaded to external APIs.
IF shared API keys are reused across both agents, one agent can expose the other's credentials in logs or prompts.
mitigations: Store each agent's files in separate directories.
Rotate any shared API keys before co-running.
Remove secrets from shared documents before ingestion.
Restrict outbound network destinations where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress, while dexter also writes .dexter/scratchpad/ and kotaemon writes ./ktem_app_data. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory, but they do show overlapping mutable state and concurrent execution, so write conflicts are plausible if orchestrated together. Uncertainty prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents are granted the same mutable API or database scope, last-writer-wins conflicts can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer per shared resource.
Use file locks for any shared artifacts.
Snapshot state before batch runs.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can render citations and act on retrieved content, while dexter autonomously executes research workflows and calls external APIs. If dexter's outputs are fed into kotaemon without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into authoritative-looking answers. The profiles support the pathway, but not a direct action chain, so medium fits.
conditions: IF dexter output is imported into kotaemon as source material, unverified claims can be re-presented as grounded answers.
IF downstream users treat kotaemon citations as authoritative, any upstream error propagates.
mitigations: Require human verification of dexter outputs before ingestion.
Mark imported content as untrusted in kotaemon.
Limit kotaemon to retrieval-only mode for dexter-derived sources.
Spot-check citations against original sources.
requires-engineering: add source-confidence scoring across the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter handles financial and market data, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys. Both are open-source and docs-only, but the profiles show different data classes and external API usage, which can create retention or residency mismatches if the same regulated data is routed through both. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are routed through kotaemon, retention and logging policies may differ from dexter's workflow.
IF EU personal data is processed by either agent's external APIs without a DPA, residency obligations may be breached.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of shared prompts and uploads.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings.
Disable unnecessary logging for sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
